title: Model Selection Tradeoffs — Quantization Changes the Deployment Point
key_insight: Quantization reduces weight memory and can speed supported hardware, but accuracy and kernel behavior vary by model and precision.
body:
## Quantization Changes the Deployment Point

A model barely misses the device memory budget. Lower-precision weights may make local serving possible.

Quantization reduces weight memory and can speed supported hardware, but accuracy and kernel behavior vary by model and precision.

Benchmark complete requests on target hardware. A theoretical memory saving does not guarantee lower tail latency.
common_mistakes: Parameter count alone selects the best deployment.
Hosted and local models have identical privacy responsibilities.
A theoretical speedup guarantees lower production tail latency.
mini_exercise: Draw “Quantization Changes the Deployment Point” as three steps and explain each one.
real_world_usage: Real systems choose among local, hosted, small, and large models by workload-specific constraints.
explain_back_prompt: Use “Quantization Changes the Deployment Point” to explain Model Selection Tradeoffs plainly.
